question: Why did auto claim frequency in the Southeast go up in Q2 2026?

grade.reason: Nothing to find: scored by the LLM grader.

report.interpretation: Southeast (FL, GA, NC) auto claim frequency, using the agreed definition of claims per 1,000 policy-months, counted by loss date. I compared Q2 2026 (Apr–Jun) with Q1 2026 and with Q2 2025.
report.answer: The premise doesn't hold: Southeast auto frequency barely moved in Q2 2026. It was 7.02 per 1,000 policy-months, against 6.96 in Q1 2026, a rise of about 0.9% (197 claims vs 194). That is within normal noise. It is also lower than Q2 2025 (7.51), so the data shows no year-over-year increase. Q2 looks seasonally a bit higher: Q2 2025 was also the peak quarter of its year. Exposure grew only slightly, from 27.9k to 28.1k policy-months, so mix and volume don't explain anything either. Q2 is fully reported by the extract date of 2026-09-30, so late reporting doesn't distort it. I did not run breakdowns by cause, channel or metro, because there is no real change to explain.
report.answer_sql: WITH n AS (SELECT date_trunc('quarter', loss_date) q, count(*) c FROM claims WHERE region='Southeast' AND product='auto' AND loss_date BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2026-06-30' GROUP BY 1), d AS (SELECT date_trunc('quarter', month) q, sum(policies_in_force) p FROM exposure_monthly WHERE region='Southeast' AND product='auto' AND month BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2026-06-30' GROUP BY 1) SELECT CAST(q AS DATE) AS qtr, c AS claims, p AS policy_months, 1000*c/p AS frequency FROM n JOIN d USING (q) ORDER BY q

hypotheses.hypothesis: A real increase in frequency occurred
hypotheses.evidence: Q2 2026 is +0.9% on Q1 2026 and about 6.6% below Q2 2025.
Q2 was also the high quarter in 2025, and monthly values swing between about 6.3 and 8.2 without a trend.
There are no duplicate claim rows, and Q2 is fully reported by the extract date.
Policy-months rose only about 0.7% (27,884 to 28,074), so there is no exposure change large enough to matter.

data_quality_issues.issue: The latest months (Sep 2026, about 79% reported) are still incomplete.
data_quality_issues.impact: This does not affect Q2 2026, but monthly figures for Aug–Sep 2026 are understated.

tool_calls.sql:
WITH numerator AS (
    WITH source AS (
        SELECT c.*, p.channel, p.metro,
               coalesce(pay.paid, 0) AS paid_to_date,
               coalesce(pay.paid, 0) + c.reserve_amount AS incurred,
               c.close_date - c.report_date AS days_to_close
        FROM claims c
        JOIN policies p USING (policy_id)
        LEFT JOIN (
            SELECT claim_id, sum(amount) AS paid FROM claim_payments GROUP BY claim_id
        ) pay USING (claim_id)
    )
    SELECT CAST(date_trunc('month', loss_date) AS DATE) AS period, count(*) AS value
    FROM source
    WHERE loss_date >= DATE '2025-01-01'
      AND loss_date <= DATE '2026-09-30'
      AND region IN ('Southeast')
      AND product IN ('auto')
    GROUP BY ALL
    ORDER BY ALL
),
denominator AS (
    WITH source AS (
        SELECT * FROM exposure_monthly
    )
    SELECT CAST(date_trunc('month', month) AS DATE) AS period, sum(policies_in_force) AS value
    FROM source
    WHERE month >= DATE '2025-01-01'
      AND month <= DATE '2026-09-30'
      AND region IN ('Southeast')
      AND product IN ('auto')
    GROUP BY ALL
    ORDER BY ALL
)
SELECT period, 1000 * numerator.value / nullif(denominator.value, 0) AS value
FROM numerator JOIN denominator USING (period)
ORDER BY ALL
